Independent final production review

The read-only reviewer checked main.c, background.c and app.c against the
immutable baseline and found no new blocking defect. Reviewed shared hashes:
main.c 157687391325be113b50a10d6abc4bca1c8f998a4ccf4e938278b60d0cd48d61
background.c 9fce6674e589a36b226e448bb7054fcdd32de255877ca7a307d084d79c652dab
app.c 4a523eb4df027616b32dc60bdcee50be0b34e4efb4b4e3c31a2d08d162fbda46

Checks covered standard descriptor preservation and race failure, background
ownership checks before first setup and fork with managed re-detach preserved,
different-host CLI identity reset, final SASL precedence, destination-scoped
old-nick control privacy, and matching fixture claims. The CA loader was also
reviewed independently for pinned reads, cleanup, trust object references,
duplicate handling and prompt refusal without a new defect being identified.

The bouncer reviewer checked the release report against final result JSONs:
10/24 baseline CAP failures, 6/14 baseline old-nick failures, 32 final executions
of eight corpora across two products and two modes. No material overclaim was
found; the draft CHATHISTORY reference was clarified. No review changes to
production source were needed. These reviews supplement, not replace, the
executed regressions and their documented platform limits.

IRC CORE / BOUNCER SECURITY REVIEW - 2026-11-16

Scope

Reviewed the shared app.c, app.h, protocol.c and protocol.h in the immutable
vipirc 0.7.29 and onekeyirc 0.1.28 baselines. Fixes are mirrored in candidate
vipirc 0.7.30 and onekeyirc 0.1.29. The review covers wire parsing, CAP/SASL
state, BATCH/playback, server-time, own-message handling, membership recovery,
private bouncer controls, bounded state, and adjacent credential/log paths.
TLS implementation, local filesystem/IPC, terminal/DCC and release packaging
have separate review owners; this note does not claim their results.

The bouncer implementation is already substantial for a per-network terminal
client: explicit ZNC and soju profiles; verified-TLS credential gates; ZNC
account/client/network PASS composition; soju SASL identity composition;
separate offered, pending and active capability sets; optional server-time,
batch, multi-prefix and ZNC self-message; restored bouncer JOINs without
replaying saved joins; bounded nested/interleaved playback; private paced
control commands; automatic-away opt-in; and staged connection identity.
No broad new bouncer feature subsystem was justified by this review.

Two changes

1. Honor the final SASL mechanism declaration in CAP LS.

The baseline returned success on the first PLAIN offer in an LS line and
kept that bit forever across continuation lines. A later sasl=EXTERNAL or
sasl= therefore could not remove an earlier PLAIN offer. The client would
request SASL despite the final declared mechanism list excluding PLAIN.
The CAP specification makes the final occurrence authoritative [1].

Both immutable baselines fail 10 out of 24 deterministic cases. Cases cover
direct SASL and soju, single and multiline lists, bare SASL, empty lists,
exact mechanism names, unrelated continuations and reverse ordering.
There were zero credential reads before ACK/challenge in these failures.
This is an authentication-state/availability correction; it is not evidence
of credential disclosure, an authentication bypass or code execution.

The scanner now distinguishes no SASL declaration (-1), an explicit list
without PLAIN (0), and an accepted offer (1). Each declaration replaces the
previous declaration; an unrelated continuation preserves it. Required
SASL fails closed before reading a credential if the final list lacks PLAIN.

2. Preserve private control handling across historical nick changes.

The prior bouncer-control fix suppressed incoming control copies only when
the sender nick equaled the client's current nick. A history message may
retain an earlier nickname; the IRCv3 history specification explicitly
warns about this [2]. An old-nick control addressed to *sasl or BouncerServ
could fall through to ordinary display and persistent logging.

The deterministic test registers, changes tester to newtester, then feeds
syntactically valid history with a fake control-secret canary under tester,
an earlier-session nickname, or an unknown batch reference. Both immutable
baselines retain the canary in display history and a private temporary log
in all six of those mode/case combinations. Eight control cases pass:
current-nick control copies remain hidden, service replies remain visible
without logging, and ordinary live/history peer messages remain visible
and logged. Total: 14 cases, six baseline failures per application.

This is a specific residual boundary of prior control-message protection,
not a repetition of the already-fixed current-nick reflection issue. It
requires the bouncer to deliver a control transcript under an old nickname.
The test establishes client behavior for that valid historical shape; no
claim is made that a tested live ZNC/soju deployment stores such transcripts.
It concerns unintended retention in the user's own log/display, not a
demonstrated ability for another IRC user to read that private log.

The fix classifies private control copies by the service destination of
the selected bouncer profile, independent of sender nickname. It does not
interpret incoming messages as commands. Normal service-source replies
retain their visible/no-persistent-log behavior, and ordinary peer messages
retain normal display/history/log behavior.

Independent bounded state checks

test_bouncer_state_properties.c uses a table of capability semantics and a
separate batch-parent/history model rather than reproducing implementation
branches. It executes 1,024 deterministic CAP sequences, each with up to
four LS lines and eight tokens per line; it checks final offer state and
that no credential is read during advertisement processing. BATCH coverage
executes 7,484 state-changing or display operations over nested/interleaved
history and unknown vendor types, plus 13 deliberately invalid frames.
The loop has 8,192 iterations; 708 attempted closes of parents with live
children are skipped instead of sending invalid input in the valid model.

Assertions check inherited history, exact active references, unknown-ref
display-only behavior, historical DCC-offer/PART/PING suppression, live
actions, visible history markers, fixed active-batch limits, queue/buffer/
log bounds, and cleared connection/queue/batch state after invalid framing.
No real DCC socket or public IRC connection is involved.

Existing tests were also run for broad app behavior, credential-log privacy,
bouncer CAP/auth/playback/control behavior, 40,000 hostile wire inputs,
91,184 exact-allocation/truncation protocol cases and 25,000 deterministic
randomized protocol cases. Counts describe test inputs, not independent
vulnerabilities found or a proof that all inputs are safe.

Validation evidence and reproduction

All baseline failures, commands, source hashes and output are retained:

  cap-baseline-results.json
  oldnick-baseline-results.json
  run_cap_reproduction.py
  run_control_reproduction.py
  test_cap_sasl_final.c
  test_bouncer_oldnick_privacy.c

The two evidence test sources are byte-identical to the new candidate tests.
All credentials/canaries are deliberately fake. Private temporary canary
logs are read by the test and removed afterward. No account, public IRC
network, password manager or external credential helper was used.

Normal and sanitizer commands/results are captured by run_bouncer_checks.py
in each application's *-results.json files. Candidate final runs use the
suffix -final for normal checks and -final-no-lsan for ASan/UBSan checks.
Each result records compiler arguments, source hashes, complete stdout/
stderr, exit status, working directory, sanitizer options and run command.
The compiler is Debian GCC 14.2.0 (14.2.0-19).

Final observed result: eight binaries per candidate passed normally and
under ASan/UBSan with leak detection disabled: 32 successful final binary
executions in total. The final 24-case CAP test and 14-case old-nick privacy
test both report zero failures. The state model and existing broader tests
also report success. No sanitizer finding was emitted in those final runs.

Initial ASan/UBSan executions with LeakSanitizer enabled abort at leak-scan
teardown because the managed environment does not allow LeakSanitizer's
thread/ptrace scanning. Those original failures are preserved in the plain
*-sanitize-results.json files. The final sanitizer run disables only leak
detection (detect_leaks=0); address and undefined-behavior checks remain
enabled with halt_on_error. Leak checking is unavailable here and is not
reported as passed.

Production/test changes (identical relative files in both candidates)

  src/app.c
  tests/test_cap_sasl_final.c
  tests/test_bouncer_state_properties.c
  tests/test_bouncer_oldnick_privacy.c

No changes were needed in protocol.c/protocol.h. app.h version macros were
left for the release owner. The reviewer did not edit Makefile.in; the
release owner is adding the three new binaries to normal/sanitizer gates.
These fixture-based tests link app.c, autocommands.c, sim.c and protocol.c
with -Isrc -Itests; like test_bouncer_core, they do not use ONEKEY_ONLY.

Limits

The evidence is deterministic core testing and source review, not live
interoperability certification, penetration testing of IRCNOW, a formal
proof, or a guarantee of freedom from vulnerabilities. No public bouncer
was contacted. Real TLS/socket integration, supported-OS terminal behavior,
and release-package gates belong to the other review workstreams. Optional
capabilities announced dynamically through CAP NEW remain deferred until
reconnect, as before. The client still uses automatic playback rather than
implementing full draft/chathistory pagination, multi-network discovery or
a remote administration dashboard.

Primary protocol references (retrieved 2026-11-16)

[1] IRCv3 Client Capability Negotiation
    https://ircv3.net/specs/extensions/capability-negotiation
    Capability lists are processed left to right; final values take priority.

[2] IRCv3 chathistory extension (draft command; ratified history batch type)
    https://ircv3.net/specs/extensions/chathistory
    Implementation Considerations explicitly covers changed historical
    source/target nicknames. This client does not request the draft command.

[3] IRCv3 batch extension
    https://ircv3.net/specs/extensions/batch
    Reference grammar, case sensitivity and parent tags on nested boundaries.

[4] IRCv3 message-tags extension
    https://ircv3.net/specs/extensions/message-tags
    Case-sensitive keys, last duplicate value and client-only tag namespace.

[5] IRCv3 SASL 3.1
    https://ircv3.net/specs/extensions/sasl-3.1
    Capability/registration sequencing and AUTHENTICATE chunk framing.

[6] IRCv3 server-time
    https://ircv3.net/specs/extensions/server-time
    Validated remote timestamps are display metadata, not local deadlines.

LOCAL PROCESS, CREDENTIAL, CONFIGURATION AND SESSION REVIEW
2026-11-16

Scope

Reviewed the shared credentials.c, config.c and background.c implementations,
their headers, and relevant main/frontend callers in the verified vipirc
0.7.29 / onekeyirc 0.1.28 baselines and the 0.7.30 / 0.1.29 candidates.
Read the earlier scoped security and bouncer reports first. Previously fixed
issues are regression coverage here, not new findings.

Two new local-process defects were reproduced. Neither is a demonstrated
remote IRC exploit. Both depend on unusual launcher/process state and are
fixed without changing verified TLS, credential, terminal-signal, or session
authentication defaults.

1. First-detach cancellation could act on an automatically reaped child PID

background_detach() originally forked its initial worker without checking the
SIGCHLD policy. Its startup-failure path subsequently used kill(child,
SIGKILL) and waitpid(child). With SIGCHLD ignored or SA_NOCLDWAIT enabled, a
failed child can already be automatically reaped before that cancellation;
its numeric PID no longer identifies an owned waitable child.

The immutable baseline reproduction uses real signal dispositions, forks,
pipes, child exit and waitpid. A setsid failure is injected only into the
test's own startup child. A poll wrapper waits for that child to disappear
under automatic reaping. The kill wrapper records and suppresses the attempted
signal. No PID reuse is forced and no unrelated process is signaled.

Both baselines admitted all three automatic-reaping policies and attempted
the stale-PID signal. Changing to SIG_IGN after preparation exposed the same
failure. Default SIGCHLD and a non-reaping notification handler retained
waitable ownership and safely collected the failed child.

Fix: background_prepare() checks child ownership before first-time setup;
background_detach() checks again immediately before pipe/fork startup. The
check rejects SIG_IGN and SA_NOCLDWAIT without changing the caller's signal
policy. Existing managed workers bypass this first-fork requirement and can
still re-detach. The public header states that callers must not independently
reap the startup child.

Final focused regression: seven cases per build, passing for both products
in normal and AddressSanitizer/UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer builds. Baseline
runs retain the four expected unsafe-policy failures.

Evidence: background-ownership-baseline.json, background-ownership-final.json,
test_background_ownership.c, and the preserved initial fixture. The final
fixture suppresses every nonzero signal under automatic reaping, including
the hypothetical case of PID reuse between observations. Earlier recorded
baseline runs all observed ESRCH and suppressed their signal attempts; the
initial fixture is retained to make the original hashes reproducible.

2. Closed standard fds could alias retained background-directory descriptors

main() originally did not reserve missing stdin/stdout/stderr descriptors.
Background endpoint preparation could therefore allocate application-owned
directory handles in slots 0, 1 or 2. Terminal quieting deliberately replaces
those standard slots with /dev/null.

The exact baseline descriptor-allocation reproduction invokes production
background_prepare() and quiet_terminal() with all eight combinations of
closed standard descriptors. It uses a separate temporary registry, real
private files, directories and socketpairs, and pathname bind/listen doubles.
No live job registry, public network or real IRC connection is used.

In all three cases with exactly two closed standard descriptors, the retained
registry descriptor was overwritten. With all three closed, both registry
and job-directory descriptors were overwritten. In this exact path the lease
and listener descriptors were preserved. Do not describe this reproduction as
proof that the listener, lease or IRC connection was lost. The confirmed
effect is corrupted ownership of retained directory handles and broken
pathname cleanup; related use of standard slots for application-owned state
is the underlying boundary failure.

Fix: main() now reserves missing standard slots before locale/options,
configuration, output or session setup. It preserves every inherited open
descriptor and its flags. Only F_GETFD failures with EBADF are replaced, using
/dev/null opened O_RDWR with close-on-exec clear. Because the scan is ascending
at process entry, open must return the exact missing slot. If it returns a
different descriptor, the helper closes only that newly opened descriptor and
fails rather than dup2 over another owner's handle. Inspection and open
failures stop startup before configuration access. Existing privilege and
core-dump protections still precede configuration/credential loading.

The shipped regression exercises the real main() entry, stopping at a config
observer before any actual configuration read. Its 18 cases cover all eight
closed-fd masks; inherited access, O_NONBLOCK, O_APPEND and FD_CLOEXEC flags;
the informational path with all standard fds closed; and inspection failure,
open failure, and a simulated intervening descriptor allocation at each slot.
All candidate cases pass normal and ASan/UBSan builds in both products.
Both immutable baselines fail the expected missing-reservation cases.

Evidence: closed-fds-baseline.json, test_background_closed_fds.c,
standard-fds-final.json, standard-fds-stable-repeats.json,
run_standard_fds.py, and test_standard_fds.c. The initial fixture/results are
retained separately: two original allocation-race assertions incorrectly
required the temporary fd to be >= 3 even while later standard slots remained
closed. Correcting that fixture required no production change. Two passing
builds observed concurrent source edits; their stable repeats are recorded
separately rather than overwriting the original observations.

Other reviewed boundaries

- Credential readers require owned regular files and strict secret modes,
  refuse symlink traversal, impose file/output/status/line bounds, reject
  malformed text, and wipe temporary plaintext. Existing tests exercise
  permissions, FIFO/symlink rejection, oversized/malformed data, cancellation,
  slot reuse, closed standard fds in helper isolation, and descendant cleanup.
- GPG starts through fixed execve argument arrays after descriptor/signal
  isolation. New encrypted credentials use private owned directories,
  bounded authenticated helper output, no-clobber publication, directory
  identity checks, and identity/content checks before cancel-time removal.
- Configuration reads are bounded and candidate-based; writes use private
  temporary files and atomic replacement. Profile names are restricted and
  catalog writes serialized. No additional defect was confirmed in these
  reviewed paths. No changes to credentials.c or config.c were justified.
- Session IPC validates peer ownership, packet framing, token identity,
  terminal descriptor types and access modes, bounded ancillary transfers,
  and terminal/controller state. Close/detach wait for completion, retain
  job identity until teardown, and never signal a job PID through the CLI.
  Existing ownership, malformed request, fd cleanup and control tests pass.

Validation summary

regressions.json records 36 successful runs: nine suites, normal and
ASan/UBSan, for both products. Suites are test_background_ownership,
test_background_control, test_background_rights,
test_security_background_output, test_credentials,
test_credential_signals, test_credential_descendants,
test_credential_lifecycle and test_config. These are concrete existing
regressions plus the new first-detach guard, not 36 separate vulnerabilities.

The tightened ownership fixture was then rerun separately in both products
and both build modes. The new standard-fd fixture was also run separately in
both products and both modes. Exact compiler commands, environment options,
source/test SHA-256 hashes, return codes and full outputs are retained in the
JSON evidence. Sanitized runs use detect_leaks=0:halt_on_error=1 and
UBSAN halt_on_error=1:print_stacktrace=1. LeakSanitizer was not enabled.

Execution and review limits

- Linux/GCC execution only. No native OpenBSD execution or complete curses
  terminal lifecycle is claimed by this local review.
- Native pathname AF_UNIX creation was unavailable in this environment.
  Native socketpair/SCM_RIGHTS tests do run; pathname listener/control tests
  use explicit doubles. Do not equate them with a native session lifecycle.
- GPG helper regressions use temporary executable fixtures, not the user's
  GPG keyring or a live credential. Real GPG cryptographic interoperability
  was not rerun by this child review.
- No public IRC, ZNC or soju server was contacted. Bouncer wire/TLS reviews,
  transport changes, DCC review, and final release-wide gates are separate
  work owned by the parent/other reviewers.
- Same-UID malicious processes, a compromised OS/GPG executable, and slow
  or hung kernel filesystem operations are not isolated by this client.
  A finite review and bounded regression set cannot establish absence of
  all vulnerabilities.

Changed files owned by this review

In both candidate products:
  src/background.c: first-detach child-ownership guard.
  src/background.h: startup ownership contract.
  src/main.c: earliest standard-descriptor reservation only; the parent's
              separate bouncer override adjustment shares this file.
  tests/test_background_ownership.c: seven ownership/state regressions.
  tests/test_standard_fds.c: eighteen startup descriptor/failure regressions.

Final candidate file hashes are recorded in local-changes-SHA256.txt. Build

RUNTIME / DCC SECURITY REVIEW - 2026-11-16

Scope

Candidates: vipirc-0.7.30 and onekeyirc-0.1.29.
Immutable reference releases: vipirc-0.7.29 and onekeyirc-0.1.28.
Reviewed dcc.c/h, dcc_commands.c/h, editor.c/h and nicks.c/h, plus read-only
review of the relevant idle.c and vipirc ui.c output/input/history paths.
Read the prior deep/follow-up security reports so old fixes are not counted
as new findings. Independently reviewed root's new net.c custom-CA loader.

Result

No new exploitable DCC/editor/nickname-completion defect was confirmed in
this sub-review. No production source change was made by this sub-review.
Two complementary test fixtures were added identically to both candidates.
These passed the immutable vipirc reference and both current candidates.
The common modules and both new tests have matching candidate hashes in
frozen-owned-source-sha256.json. net.c and other read-only source hashes in
that snapshot identify the reviewed revision, not ownership or a promise
that the parent will make no later changes.

Reviewed invariants

- Incoming DCC parsing is bounded by IRC_BODY_MAX, rejects extensions,
  malformed/overflowing numbers and unsafe filenames, and performs no I/O.
- Offers/active transfers/retained entries are limited to 8/4/12. Acceptance
  is explicit. Stable transfer IDs and fd matching reject stale poll events.
- Receive destinations use private directory checks, descriptor-relative
  no-follow/exclusive creation, and inode/device checks before failed-transfer
  unlink. Source selection is pinned to the opened file identity.
- Per-turn network DCC progress and ACK processing are bounded. Pending ACK
  output suppresses input polling; duplicate ACKs do not extend idle timeout.
- Receive/send arithmetic stays within the advertised uint32_t size. Peer
  ACKs must be monotonic and no greater than bytes sent.
- Editor UTF-8 rejection is transactional; character/byte limits, cursor
  and wrapping loops remain bounded. Nick completion validates ASCII IRC
  nicknames and replacement character/byte capacity before moving data.
- Idle output is sanitized, retained and queued with byte/count limits,
  nonblocking writes and bounded flush work. Frame-capacity fallbacks avoid
  a redraw loop when a display does not fit. Disk history reads remain
  bounded to the captured file range and sanitize each record before output.

New test: tests/test_runtime_guard_pages.c

Input NUL and exact output capacities end immediately before PROT_NONE.
Cases include every non-NUL one-byte/two-byte sequence in editor input and
DCC filenames; truncated Unicode/IRC formatting/terminal-control and DCC
syntax prefixes; 255/256-byte filenames; parser body boundaries; editor
character/byte capacity boundaries; successful round trips; transactional
failure; and extreme navigation coordinates on accepted input.

One execution reports 65,881 DCC cases (10,373 accepted) and 65,881 editor
cases (11,638 accepted). The repeated normal/sanitizer/product runs exercise
the same corpus; they are not additional distinct test cases.

New test: tests/test_dcc_counter_edges.c

The fixture seeds already-completed progress near UINT32_MAX and moves the
remaining 1, 3, 16,383, 16,384 or 16,385 bytes through native AF_UNIX
socketpairs and private newly created regular files. It checks both maximum
advertised sizes UINT32_MAX-1 and UINT32_MAX. It validates byte-exact tails,
high-bit ACK values with 1/2/1-byte fragmentation, monotonic counters,
rejection of wrapped/backward/too-large ACKs and immediately detectable
receive overrun, descriptor cleanup, failed-file removal, and exhausted
uint64_t IDs refusing reuse.

One execution reports 20 completed tails, 6 rejected malformed peers and
196,624 actual payload bytes. This is state-boundary testing, not a claim of
a native complete 4 GiB transfer or public TCP interoperability testing.

Validation and retained failures

Exact compiler/runtime argv, environment, working directory, complete
stdout/stderr, source hashes, exit status and elapsed time are stored in
per-command .json/.log files. run.py refuses to overwrite earlier evidence.

- Immutable vipirc-0.7.29: both tests compiled with strict warnings and
  passed in normal builds before candidate testing.
- vipirc-0.7.30 and onekeyirc-0.1.29: both tests compiled with
  -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror in normal and ASan/UBSan modes.
- Both candidates: both tests passed normal execution and ASan/UBSan with
  halt_on_error=1, UBSan stack traces enabled, and detect_leaks=0.
- The four initial sanitizer runs with detect_leaks=1 failed at LeakSanitizer
  shutdown with its fatal ptrace/environment restriction. These failures
  remain in *-san-run.json/log. They are not reported as successful runs and
  are not a confirmed application leak. No LeakSanitizer coverage is claimed.
- Native fixture assertions explicitly verify closure of the descriptors
  they own and failed receive-file cleanup; these do not replace heap-leak
  analysis.

Independent custom-CA loader review

Reviewed load_ca_file/ca_store_added as introduced by the parent in net.c.
No new cleanup/trust-policy defect was identified by this read-only review.
The single checked descriptor, regular-file/16 MiB bound, size+1 read,
explicit noninteractive PEM callback, memory BIO/object/byte cleanup order,
per-add OpenSSL error clearing and destruction of failed partial TLS contexts
were checked. Parent owns its implementation, differential tests and final
results. This sub-review does not substitute for those tests.

Limits and outstanding observations

- Classic DCC remains unencrypted and unauthenticated. An outgoing listener
  accepts its first connecting peer. These are documented protocol limits,
  not newly fixed vulnerabilities.
- Regular-file reads/writes/logging can still wait on slow filesystems.
  Neither O_NONBLOCK nor a byte bound provides a filesystem wall-clock limit.
- The custom-CA byte bound is not a measured wall-clock or decoded-object
  memory bound for every supported TLS library.
- vipirc's full curses frontend still writes via newterm(stdout, stdin) and
  doupdate without idle.c's nonblocking output queue. Source review suggests
  a stalled terminal may hold its loop. Actual full-screen reproduction was
  not performed here, so this remains an unvalidated availability limitation,
  not a new confirmed security finding. No speculative UI rewrite was made.
- No live IRC network/bouncer, public listener, real credential, existing
  user file/session, full 4 GiB transfer, or full-screen curses integration
  was used by these fixtures. Native AF_UNIX socketpairs, private temporary
  files and protected anonymous memory were used.
- Passing finite tests and source review is not a claim that either client
  is invulnerable.

import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
WORK = ROOT.parents[1]
TESTS = ("test_cap_sasl_final", "test_bouncer_oldnick_privacy", "test_bouncer_state_properties", "test_bouncer_core",
         "test_security_state", "test_security_auth", "test_app", "test_protocol")

def sha(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--tree", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--mode", choices=("normal", "sanitize"), required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--label", default="")
    parser.add_argument("--no-leaks", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--tests", nargs="+", choices=TESTS, default=list(TESTS))
    args = parser.parse_args()
    tree = WORK / "security-next-work" / args.tree
    records = []
    result_file = ROOT / (args.tree + "-" + args.mode + args.label + "-results.json")
    assert not result_file.exists(), "Do not overwrite initial validation results"
    env = dict(os.environ)
    if args.mode == "sanitize":
        env["ASAN_OPTIONS"] = ("detect_leaks=0" if args.no_leaks else "detect_leaks=1") + ":halt_on_error=1:abort_on_error=1"
        env["UBSAN_OPTIONS"] = "halt_on_error=1:print_stacktrace=1"
    flags = ["-std=c11", "-Wall", "-Wextra", "-Wpedantic"]
    flags += (["-O2"] if args.mode == "normal" else
              ["-O1", "-g", "-fsanitize=address,undefined", "-fno-omit-frame-pointer", "-fno-pie", "-no-pie"])
    for name in args.tests:
        binary = ROOT / (args.tree + "-" + args.mode + args.label + "-" + name)
        sources = ["tests/" + name + ".c", "src/protocol.c"]
        if name != "test_protocol":
            sources += ["src/app.c", "src/autocommands.c", "src/sim.c"]
        command = ["cc"] + flags + ["-Isrc", "-Itests"] + sources + ["-o", str(binary)]
        build = subprocess.run(command, cwd=tree, text=True, capture_output=True, timeout=180)
        record = {"test": name, "cwd": str(tree), "command": command,
                  "source_sha256": {p: sha(tree / p) for p in sources + ["src/app.h", "src/protocol.h", "tests/test_app.c"]},
                  "compile": {"returncode": build.returncode, "stdout": build.stdout, "stderr": build.stderr}}
        if build.returncode == 0:
            record["environment"] = {k: env[k] for k in ("ASAN_OPTIONS", "UBSAN_OPTIONS") if k in env}
            record["run_command"] = [str(binary)]
            try:
                run = subprocess.run([str(binary)], cwd=tree, text=True, capture_output=True, env=env, timeout=180)
                record["run"] = {"returncode": run.returncode, "stdout": run.stdout, "stderr": run.stderr}
                print(args.tree, args.mode, name, "exit", run.returncode, flush=True)
                print(run.stdout + run.stderr, end="", flush=True)
            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as exc:
                record["run"] = {"returncode": "timeout", "stdout": str(exc.stdout), "stderr": str(exc.stderr)}
                print(args.tree, args.mode, name, "TIMEOUT", flush=True)
        else:
            print(args.tree, args.mode, name, "BUILD FAILED", build.stderr, flush=True)
        records.append(record)
        result_file.write_text(json.dumps(records, indent=2) + "\n")
    assert all(r["compile"]["returncode"] == 0 and r["run"]["returncode"] == 0 for r in records)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

        flags += ['-O1', '-g', '-fsanitize=address,undefined', '-fno-omit-frame-pointer', '-fno-pie', '-no-pie'] if mode == 'asan-ubsan' else ['-O2']
        test = validation / 'test_standard_fds.c'
        command = ['cc', *flags, *defines, '-Isrc', str(test), *sources, '-lssl', '-lcrypto', '-o', str(output)]
        def hashes():
            paths = sorted(set(sources + ['src/main.c']) | {str(path.relative_to(root)) for path in (root/'src').glob('*.h')})
            return {path: hashlib.sha256((root/path).read_bytes()).hexdigest() for path in paths}
        before = hashes()
        compiled = subprocess.run(command, cwd=root, text=True, capture_output=True)
        after = hashes()
        run = subprocess.run([str(output)], cwd=root, text=True, capture_output=True,
                             env=environment, timeout=25) if compiled.returncode == 0 else None
        record = {'product': product, 'state': state, 'mode': mode, 'cwd': str(root),
                  'compile_command': command, 'compile_returncode': compiled.returncode,
                  'compile_stdout': compiled.stdout, 'compile_stderr': compiled.stderr,
                  'source_sha256_before': before, 'source_sha256_after': after,
                  'sources_unchanged_during_build': before == after,
                  'fixture_sha256': hashlib.sha256(test.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
                  'run_command': [str(output)],
                  'environment': {key: environment[key] for key in ['ASAN_OPTIONS', 'UBSAN_OPTIONS']},
                  'run_returncode': run.returncode if run else None,
                  'stdout': run.stdout if run else None, 'stderr': run.stderr if run else None}
        records.append(record)
        (validation / 'standard-fds-final.json').write_text(json.dumps(records, indent=2) + '\n')
        print(f'{product} {state} {mode}: compile={compiled.returncode} run={run.returncode if run else None} stable={before == after}', flush=True)
        if compiled.returncode or not run or run.returncode != (1 if state == 'baseline' else 0):
            print(compiled.stderr, run.stdout if run else '', run.stderr if run else '', flush=True)
raise SystemExit(0 if all(record['compile_returncode'] == 0 and
    record['run_returncode'] == (1 if record['state'] == 'baseline' else 0) and
    record['sources_unchanged_during_build'] for record in records) else 1)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Preserve exact validation commands and outcomes, including failures."""
import datetime
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import shlex
import subprocess
import sys
import time

root = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
label, directory, *command = sys.argv[1:]
if not command or not label.replace("-", "").replace("_", "").isalnum():
    raise SystemExit("usage: run.py label working-directory command [args...]")
cwd = Path(directory).resolve()
log = root / (label + ".log")
metadata = root / (label + ".json")
if log.exists() or metadata.exists():
    raise SystemExit("Refusing to overwrite evidence for " + label)
start = time.monotonic()
record = {
    "label": label,
    "utc_started": datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat(),
    "cwd": str(cwd),
    "argv": command,
    "shell_equivalent": shlex.join(command),
    "timeout_seconds": 60,
    "environment": {k: os.environ[k] for k in
                    ("ASAN_OPTIONS", "UBSAN_OPTIONS", "LC_ALL", "LC_CTYPE") if k in os.environ},
    "source_sha256": {},
}
for area in ("src", "tests"):
    for file in sorted((cwd / area).glob("*")):
        if file.is_file() and file.suffix in (".c", ".h"):
            record["source_sha256"][str(file.relative_to(cwd))] = hashlib.sha256(file.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
for argument in command:
    file = Path(argument)
    if not file.is_absolute():
        file = cwd / file
    if file.is_file() and (file.suffix in (".c", ".h", ".py") or os.access(file, os.X_OK)):
        record["source_sha256"][str(file.resolve())] = hashlib.sha256(file.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
try:
    result = subprocess.run(command, cwd=cwd, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                            stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, timeout=60, check=False)
    output = result.stdout
    record["exit_code"] = result.returncode
except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as error:
    output = (error.stdout or b"") + b"\nHARNESS TIMEOUT: 60 seconds\n"
    record["exit_code"] = 124
record["elapsed_seconds"] = round(time.monotonic() - start, 6)
record["output_sha256"] = hashlib.sha256(output).hexdigest()
log.write_bytes(output)
metadata.write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="ascii")
print(label + ": exit=" + str(record["exit_code"]) + " elapsed=" + str(record["elapsed_seconds"]) + "s")
print("command: " + shlex.join(command))
lines = output.decode("utf-8", "backslashreplace").splitlines()
print("\n".join(lines[:35]))
if len(lines) > 35:
    print("[full output preserved in " + str(log) + "]")
raise SystemExit(record["exit_code"] if 0 <= record["exit_code"] <= 255 else 1)
